Vels Fadhecai (Vels Fadhecai, G38)

Region (English scoring-table region): North Aelantir.

In one sentence: Begin as a three-province state in the Forest Beyond the River, let a blood mage who refuses the old order turn her home into a magical power, and watch how that transformation harms others.

Story: Very high | Mission-tree length: Medium-long (35 direct G38 missions) | Mission-tree update: use the current local scripts supporting EU4 v1.37.5.0 | Uniqueness: Very high | Grind: Medium-high (closed terrain and magical prerequisites) | Early pressure: Medium-high | Expansion: Medium-high, increasing after the forest exit opens

A three-province state in the Forest Beyond the River

In 1444 Vels Fadhecai already holds three independent provinces, and its capital is also called Vels Fadhecai. The local history sets it as a Sarda-culture, Ynnic-faith, feudal-monarchy country ruled by Celadil I of the Konyrzab family. The forest and black soil protect its towns while narrowing outside access. The later blood-mage policies of Mitrenya must not be projected backward onto Celadil's opening institutions; the mission story is about how this frontier country changes over time.【Local history script】【Local flavour text】

The offline English Wiki country page contains only an identity frame and no historical prose, so it cannot establish the year this country was founded. Current ideas and flavour text are more specific: the Sardan forest shelters the towns and receives some exiles and people who do not fit the old order. This “haven” image is a genuine opening theme, but it does not guarantee that later expansion respects everyone living elsewhere. The Halann historical map records only the 1444 three-province anchor and cannot fill its blank years with a definite imperial history.【Wiki source】【Local flavour text】

Turning the forest defence outward

Early missions acknowledge that the country is easy to defend but difficult to leave. The player must manage Sardan neighbours, the mage estate, and military advisers before the safe border can become an offensive route. The tree then moves toward other Ynnic countries, Epednar relic regions, and northern positions. Older documentation summarizes this as revenge for historical crimes and Mitrenya's rise, but exact territory, missions, and events remain governed by the current scripts; an old summary is not completed history.【Local script】【Document record】

Mitrenya's story distinguishes Vels Fadhecai from an ordinary mage country. Current English flavour begins with intimacy and court power: she refuses to let noble succession determine who may study magic, and the specialized mage faction gradually takes over the state. The missions require a “secret journey” to stabilize the capital and surroundings and complete Ynnic reforms; later, mage influence, royal land, and research restrictions become thresholds for reorganizing power. This is not a country with unlimited spellcasting at game start: magical power is exchanged for political conditions step by step.【Local flavour text】【Local script】【Document record】

The price of research

The story also has a dark side that cannot be hidden behind the phrase “rebellious heroine.” Current mission flavour explicitly says that Mitrenya does not care how knowledge is obtained and assumes that nobody will care if a few Epednar disappear; later text about removing and transplanting hearts treats other bodies as experimental material. Other passages describe “clearing” local inhabitants as an achievement, or acknowledge that even a milder religious reform may secretly take test subjects away. Branches change the surface policy and the terms used for ruled groups, but they do not erase the kidnappings and harm written into the central line.【Local flavour text】【Local script】

That is the sharp contradiction: the country shelters internal dissenters and exiles, yet may deny the intelligent inhabitants of another land the same rights. Blood magic can produce healing potions and formidable armies, and some scenes even have Mitrenya step away from day-to-day royal power and hand rule to a council of mages; technology and political organization genuinely develop, but their costs are not cancelled by achievement. The “Ynnic Empire” direction is a future political ambition; it has not been confirmed here that G38 must change into one fixed successor Tag.【Local script】【Local flavour text】【Unverified】

Players who follow the character relationships will find that intimacy and cruelty are not unrelated branches: the partner is willing to pay any price for Mitrenya's dream, while flavour events also make the narrator recognize that an expedition to an Epednar village was barbaric. This gives the character complexity, not protection for victims from experimentation. Characterization is worth reading; the value judgment still rests on how the country treats people and bodies.【Local flavour text】

Personality and recommendation

The v2.1 personality coordinates are Expansion 68/100 | Authoritarianism 78/100 | Magic ↔ Artifice 92/100 (100 = magic, 0 = artifice; theme intensity 91/100) | Pluralism 62/100. Phase change: forest haven (Pluralism 72) → Epednar experiments and conquest (Pluralism 35).

The v2.1 value is Evil (22/100), with a worsening trajectory. Phase value: forest refuge and early administration (Neutral 55/100) → kidnappings and heart experiments (Evil 22/100). Refuge, agriculture, and healing potions have public benefits; current mission text still explicitly describes secret abductions of Epednar people, using their bodies for heart research, and the dehumanizing language of clearing inhabitants. A supposedly milder reform does not automatically exclude disappearing test subjects. The source reiterates the phase change: forest refuge and early administration (Neutral 55/100) → kidnappings and heart experiments (Evil 22/100). Refuge, farming and medicine have public benefits, but abduction, research on living subjects, hearts treated as materials and dehumanising descriptions of Epednar people directly lower dignity, personhood and restraint. The score is not reduced merely because the country is a monarchy, wages war, or uses blood magic; it targets concrete victims and actions. It suits players who want a forest frontier, character relationships, blood sorcery, and an unreliable reformer narrative, and not players who need the protagonist's rebellion to represent universal liberation or who do not want human-experimentation material.【Local flavour text】

Players often call the long relationship between Mitrenya and her partner the main attraction, while also discussing mission-transition issues in old development branches and saves that had already formed the Ynnic Empire. Those posts describe player experience; they cannot prove that current G38 requires a Tag change or that a particular mission bug has been fixed.【Community view】

Detailed local line ranges, the offline Wiki stub, and two player posts are recorded in the evidence page.

National ideas (reference appendix)

The following reproduces native English national-idea names and descriptions alongside the inherited source displays. Traditions apply when the set is adopted; the seven ideas unlock with investment in idea groups, and ambition applies once all seven are unlocked. Racial, government and mission bonuses are excluded. Successor ideas do not stack automatically with the predecessor set. Descriptions may recount history or depict a future ideal, not events already completed in 1444. Native English prose is used rather than back-translating the Chinese localisation; any inherited display/unit uncertainty remains unresolved.

Vels Fadhecai (G38) — Fadhecan Ideas

Traditions: Fadhecan Traditions

Effects: shock_damage_received：-10%; Same-culture advisor cost: -15%.

Idea 1: The Book of Epadarkan

Detailing the grueling despair of the Sarda settlements that fell to the Epednar in the fourth and fifth centuries after Flood, the Book of Epadarkan is a somber reminder of what would happen to our people should we falter in front of barbarians.

Effects: War exhaustion: -0.03.

Idea 2: The Unfortunate Name

Vels Fadhecai, the Forest Beyond the River. A beautiful name, so beautiful it was copied from us three times over: not only by Vels Bacar upstream and Vels Domfan downstream, but even if we omit Vels there's Fadhevych on the other side of the Ynn… With little use arguing ours was the original name, this similarity has caused many letters and deliveries meant for Vels Fadhecai to arrive to one of the three other places, an unfortunate inconvenience which we have learned to deal with by always having a couple diplomats and canoe-couriers on standby.

Effects: Diplomats: +1; Envoy travel time: -15%.

Idea 3: Tyerna Krarh

The black soil of the Fadhecan woodlands, known as "Tyerna Krarh", is perhaps the greatest blessing our fief received, allowing our peasants to produce plentiful food over small plots of land. This has allowed our towns to never suffer a famine, and thus their inhabitants could safely focus on crafts and trades, while peasants tilled the soil under the cover of the trees.

Vels Fadhecai's forest is the thickest of Sarda, providing a natural defense from the Epednar of the plains, but our crops can nonetheless withstand the darkness thanks to ancient magic. Because of this, we've never had to deforest the land, and our towns more often than not are sprawling on the sides of trees and hanging off of their branches, unless a war causes them to be destroyed, but, in those cases, many a town have been rebuilt more beautiful than before.

Effects: Development cost: -10%.

Idea 4: Home of the Exiled Poet

Vels Fadhecai has always been the favourite location to exile dissidents to. Conspirators, disgraced knights, or just the occasional courtier who said the wrong thing at the wrong time. One such example of the latter was the poet Talvyr, who fell out of grace with Emperor Calrodiy I after jokingly calling him "the Battleking of the Ynnics".

Banished to Vels Fadhecai, Talvyr became an open dissident to Calrodiy's regime, writing poems that questioned the utility of war while in his verses he likened soldiers to brutes and knights to thugs. However, when a band of Epednar riders approached the town he was living in and he saw the local guards stand up for his protection, the seed of change was planted in Talvyr, and a year later he wrote his most famous book, "To the Garrisons".

Vels Fadhecai has seen many people arrive, from all walks of life and believing in radically different things. They all went through a similar story, a story where different people align together, and each contribute with their uniqueness, their individuality, in the face of a common threat.

Effects: Idea cost: -10%.

Idea 5: Realm of the Blood Mage

1581 marked the end of the regency for Lady Mitrenya, whose mother had died birthing her and whose father was assassinated while at a brothel. From the earliest age she showed great magical propensity, being able to conjure water bubbles and even water bombs she would hit her guardians with. When the War of the Bacaran succession erupted in 1602, Mitrenya was already a consummate war veteran, having led incursions into the Epednar territories over the past two decades, going as far as to reach the recently-founded city of Elathael during one of them.

It was thus to everyone's surprise when she announced she would maintain her neutrality during the Bacaran conflict.

Twenty years later, when the war was over, a shocking discovery was made: Mitrenya had been torturing the prisoners made during her past incursions, as well as some of her subjects and even relatives of her vassals. Not satisfied with water magic anymore, she would finish torturing them only to kill them then bathe in their blood; drawing power from it, using it to strengthen her magic and stay young forever.

With most of the Ynn still recovering from war, nobody moved to oppose Mitrenya, except for Vyr Arok yen Clovenvels, a mercenary captain of Escanni origin who ventured into the forests of Vels Fadhecai and defeated her many minions. Together with a small party of his most elite troops he snuck into Mitrenya's castle, where they slew her after a hard-fought battle.

Effects: Harsh treatment cost: -25%.

Idea 6: Let's Get Down to Business…

It is an undeniable reality that many settlements have seen their rise and prosperity west of our fair woodlands over the recent decades. Their people have more in common with us than barbarians do, and, while it is sad to see them occupy what was our ancient homeland, acknowledging their success will be a necessary step to bring new life and prosperity to our lordship. Deals will have to be made, and an outer facade of friendship will need to be maintained, as we obtain new materials and techniques, and learn any secret deemed useful.

Effects: Monthly innovativeness: +0.25; Institution embrace cost: -10%.

Idea 7: …To Defeat the Epednar

"The first thing you need to understand, is that to defeat the barbarian, you must understand the barbarian. Think, smell, and ride like barbarians do. Secondly, always do what I tell you. You, with the weak frame and the slingshot. Come over here. If you survive training, I will make you a honorary half-orc."

-Address of a Chippengarder captain hired to train Fadhecan militias

Effects: Army Drill gain modifier: +50%.
